subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals for PeakHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@peakhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@peakhealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 13:15:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals for PeakHealth

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for taking the time. Quick recap from our call so we have aligned next steps: 

Pain points you shared:
- Lack of end-to-end observability for model behavior in production (hard to trace prompt->response regressions).
- No standardized evals or golden-prompt sets to detect regressions across model updates.
- Dashboarding is manual; CS/Engs need near-real-time alerts for drift/regressions.

Current stack:
- Inference: in-house service backed by Mistral/LLM model variants running on AWS (ECS + spot GPUs).
- Logging: CloudWatch + S3; some ad-hoc traces via Datadog APM.
- CI: internal pipeline for model deploys, no automated post-deploy quality checks.

Success criteria you outlined:
- Detect regressions in QoR within 5% of baseline accuracy for critical prompts within 24 hours of a rollout.
- Dashboards for per-route latency, cost-per-token, eval scores, and a regression alerting pipeline tied to golden prompts.
- Tracing hooks so SRE can link requests back to prompt variants and model versions.

Next steps I proposed:
1) I’ll send a short proposal with recommended observability dashboard templates, tracing hookup notes, and an eval playbook (attached).
2) Loop in Marcus (our solutions SE) to scope integration work and required tracing hooks.
3) If this looks good, we can set a tech sync next week to walk through the dashboard prototype and a short PoC plan.

Attachments: observability-dashboard-proposal.pdf (dashboard templates), golden-prompts.xlsx (starter set), redwood-eval-playbook.pdf (how we run regression checks).

Does this capture everything correctly? If so, I’ll get Marcus on a quick tech sync and propose times.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@peakhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@peakhealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals for PeakHealth

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and captures the discussion. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- For success criteria, the 5% QoR delta should apply to our 3 "priority" prompts (patient triage, eligibility check, and clinical summary).
- We need the regression alerts to generate a ticket in Jira (SUP-3421) and also notify the #model-ops Slack channel.
- Tracing hooks are non-negotiable for the SRE team — we need request-level correlation ids to link logs, traces, and model metadata.

Next steps from PeakHealth:
- Priya will share the current golden prompt set and a sanitized sample of logs (we’ll send by EOD today).
- We are open to a 4-week PoC; procurement will want a short SOW and a price estimate.

Appreciate the attachments — will review and follow up. Happy to do the tech sync; Tue/Wed next week after 14:00 PT works for us.

Best,
Alex
Product Manager, PeakHealth
alex.johnson@peakhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@peakhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@peakhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 00:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals for PeakHealth

Thanks Alex — great notes. Looping in Marcus (SE) to scope the tracing hooks and dashboard integration. Marcus — quick context: PeakHealth needs 
- request-level correlation ids surfaced from their inference layer through to CloudWatch/Datadog and into our tracing UI;
- dashboard templates for per-route eval scores, latency, error-rate, and cost-per-token;
- an automated regression job that runs golden-prompts nightly and raises Jira tickets + Slack alerts when thresholds are crossed.

Marcus — can you review the attached playbook and the golden-prompts.xlsx and propose a minimal PoC workplan (estimate 2-4 days of engineering + how we’d wire the alert integrations)? We’d like to propose Wed 20th or Thu 21st at 15:00 PT for a 45-min tech sync.

Action items for us after tech sync:
- SOW + 4-week PoC pricing for procurement.
- PoC runbook with success criteria mapped to the 3 priority prompts.
- Setup of dashboards (hosted preview) and tracing hook example for PeakHealth team to test.

Thanks — I’ll also prepare a short slide for procurement that outlines deliverables and timelines.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@peakhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@peakhealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 03:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals for PeakHealth

Thanks for the context, Marissa — reviewed the attachments quickly. High-level plan for the PoC: 

1) Day 0–3: Install tracing hook example and correlation-id middleware (we’ll provide a reference patch and a short integration guide).
2) Day 4–7: Deploy dashboard templates to a hosted preview and run initial golden-prompt evaluations (we’ll ingest the sample prompts from Priya).
3) Day 8–14: Automate nightly regression jobs, wire Jira (SUP-3421) and Slack alerts, and tune thresholds with PeakHealth.

Estimate: 5 engineer-days (+1 SE for onboarding) for the minimal PoC. I can prepare a short technical SOW and a one-page integration checklist before the sync.

Proposed times: Wed 21 Oct 2026 15:00 PT (we will be ready).

I’ll attach a brief integration checklist after this thread (sending now as part of the follow-up).

Regards,
Marcus Lin
